requirements.original: When importing into a TTCN-3 module, the language specification (see clause 8.1) of the importing module, the language specification of the import statement and the language specification of the source module, where the imported definitions are defined, have to be compatible according to the following rules.
requirements.canonical: When importing into a TTCN-3 module, the language specification of the importing module, the language specification of the import statement and the language specification of the source module SHALL be compatible according to the rules of clause 8.2.3.8.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.8 -- When importing into a TTCN-3 module, the language specification (see clause 8.1) of the importing module, the language specification of the import statement and the language specification of the source module, where the imported definitions are defined, have to be compatible according to the following rules.

requirements.original: a) A TTCN-3 module of any TTCN-3 edition can import from a non-TTCN-3 language source provided that a TTCN-3 view for the non-TTCN-3 language exists (see clause 8.2.3.6).
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 module of any TTCN-3 edition MAY import from a non-TTCN-3 language source provided that a TTCN-3 view for the non-TTCN-3 language exists.
requirements.condition: a TTCN-3 view for the non-TTCN-3 language exists
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.8 -- a) A TTCN-3 module of any TTCN-3 edition can import from a non-TTCN-3 language source provided that a TTCN-3 view for the non-TTCN-3 language exists (see clause 8.2.3.6).

requirements.original: b) Definitions or import statements are imported according to the language specification in which the definition or the import statement is defined.
requirements.canonical: A definition or import statement IS imported according to the language specification of the module in which the definition or import statement is defined.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.8 -- b) Definitions or import statements are imported according to the language specification in which the definition or the import statement is defined.

requirements.original: If no language specification is given in this module, the language specification of the import statement with which those definitions or import statements are to be imported, is used instead.
requirements.canonical: If the module in which the definitions or import statements are defined has no language specification, the language specification of the import statement that imports them IS used instead.
requirements.condition: the defining module has no language specification
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.8 -- If no language specification is given in this module, the language specification of the import statement with which those definitions or import statements are to be imported, is used instead.

requirements.original: If the module, within which the definitions or the import statements are defined, and the import statement for these definitions or import statements provide both a language specification, then they shall be identical.
requirements.canonical: If both the module in which the imported definitions or import statements are defined and the import statement importing them have a language specification, these language specifications SHALL be identical.
requirements.condition: both the defining module and the import statement provide a language specification
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.8 -- If the module, within which the definitions or the import statements are defined, and the import statement for these definitions or import statements provide both a language specification, then they shall be identical.

requirements.original: c) A TTCN-3 module shall only import from earlier or same editions of TTCN-3 but not from later editions, e.g. the TTCN-3 language specification in an import statement has to be lower or equal to the TTCN-3 language specification of the importing module.
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 module SHALL NOT import from a later TTCN-3 edition than its own; it SHALL import only from earlier or the same editions.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.8 -- c) A TTCN-3 module shall only import from earlier or same editions of TTCN-3 but not from later editions, e.g. the TTCN-3 language specification in an import statement has to be lower or equal to the TTCN-3 language specification of the importing module.

requirements.original: c) A TTCN-3 module shall only import from earlier or same editions of TTCN-3 but not from later editions, e.g. the TTCN-3 language specification in an import statement has to be lower or equal to the TTCN-3 language specification of the importing module.
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language specification in an import statement SHALL be lower than or equal to the TTCN-3 language specification of the importing module.

ambiguity.issue: The rule is introduced with 'e.g.' although it restates the edition rule ('i.e.' seems meant); also the ordering of language identifiers is not explicitly defined.
readings: The import statement's TTCN-3 language specification SHALL denote an edition not later than the importing module's edition (comparison by edition date).
The comparison of language specifications is only one example; other checks of edition ordering may apply instead.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.8 -- c) A TTCN-3 module shall only import from earlier or same editions of TTCN-3 but not from later editions, e.g. the TTCN-3 language specification in an import statement has to be lower or equal to the TTCN-3 language specification of the importing module.

requirements.original: Modules can define other modules to be friends.
requirements.canonical: A module MAY define other modules to be its friend modules.

examples.text: module MyModuleA { friend module MyModuleB,MyModuleC; } // MyModuleB and MyModuleC are friends of MyModuleA module MyModuleB { friend module MyModuleA; } // MyModuleA is friend of MyModuleB module MyModuleC { }

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.4 -- Modules can define other modules to be friends.

requirements.original: [ private ] friend module ModuleIdentifier { "," ModuleIdentifier } ";"
requirements.canonical: A friend module declaration has the syntax [private] friend module ModuleIdentifier { "," ModuleIdentifier } ";".

examples.text: module MyModuleA { friend module MyModuleB,MyModuleC; } // MyModuleB and MyModuleC are friends of MyModuleA module MyModuleB { friend module MyModuleA; } // MyModuleA is friend of MyModuleB module MyModuleC { }

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.4 -- [ private ] friend module ModuleIdentifier { "," ModuleIdentifier } ";"

requirements.original: Friendship to modules is defined by the exporting module (the module that declares the definitions) not by the importing module (the module that uses the module definitions of another module).
requirements.canonical: Friendship to modules IS defined by the exporting module, which declares the definitions, and IS NOT defined by the importing module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.4 -- Friendship to modules is defined by the exporting module (the module that declares the definitions) not by the importing module (the module that uses the module definitions of another module).

requirements.original: Friendship can be cyclic.
requirements.canonical: Friendship between modules MAY be cyclic.

examples.text: module MyModuleA { friend module MyModuleB,MyModuleC; } // MyModuleB and MyModuleC are friends of MyModuleA module MyModuleB { friend module MyModuleA; } // MyModuleA is friend of MyModuleB module MyModuleC { }

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.4 -- Friendship can be cyclic.

requirements.original: If a module is friend to a module from which it imports top-level definitions, all top-level definitions with public and friend visibility are visible to the friend module.
requirements.canonical: If a module is a friend of a module from which it imports top-level definitions, all top-level definitions with `public` and `friend` visibility ARE visible to the friend module.
requirements.condition: the importing module is a friend of the exporting module
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.4 -- If a module is friend to a module from which it imports top-level definitions, all top-level definitions with public and friend visibility are visible to the friend module.

requirements.original: For non-friend modules, public top-level definitions are visible only.
requirements.canonical: For a non-friend importing module, only `public` top-level definitions ARE visible.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.4 -- For non-friend modules, public top-level definitions are visible only.

requirements.original: Missing friend modules shall not cause an error.
requirements.canonical: A friend module declaration that references a missing module SHALL NOT cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: 'Missing' is not defined: it may mean a module that does not exist at all or one that is not part of the current compilation.
readings: A friend module declaration naming a module that does not exist in the test suite SHALL NOT cause an error.
A friend module declaration naming a module that is not available to the tool in the current build SHALL NOT cause an error.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.4 -- Missing friend modules shall not cause an error.

requirements.original: NOTE: Friend modules can be checked by tools, however at most warning are to be issued if a friend module is missing.
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL NOT issue more than a warning if a friend module is missing.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.4 -- NOTE: Friend modules can be checked by tools, however at most warning are to be issued if a friend module is missing.

requirements.original: a) Only private visibility can be defined for friend definitions as they are always private.
requirements.canonical: A friend module declaration SHALL have only `private` visibility, if any visibility is specified.

ambiguity.issue: 'friend definitions' is used for friend module declarations.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.4 -- a) Only private visibility can be defined for friend definitions as they are always private.

requirements.original: a) Only private visibility can be defined for friend definitions as they are always private.
requirements.canonical: A friend module declaration IS always private.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.4 -- a) Only private visibility can be defined for friend definitions as they are always private.

requirements.original: Top-level module definitions and import statements have a visibility, which can be explicitly set.
requirements.canonical: A top-level module definition HAS a visibility.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- Top-level module definitions and import statements have a visibility, which can be explicitly set.

requirements.original: Top-level module definitions and import statements have a visibility, which can be explicitly set.
requirements.canonical: An import statement HAS a visibility.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- Top-level module definitions and import statements have a visibility, which can be explicitly set.

requirements.original: Top-level module definitions and import statements have a visibility, which can be explicitly set.
requirements.canonical: The visibility of a top-level module definition or an import statement MAY be set explicitly by a visibility modifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- Top-level module definitions and import statements have a visibility, which can be explicitly set.

requirements.original: They are by default public except for imported and friend definitions.
requirements.canonical: A top-level module definition without an explicit visibility modifier IS public by default, except for imported definitions and friend definitions.

ambiguity.issue: 'friend definitions' (definitions with explicit friend visibility) cannot be default-public, since their visibility is explicit; the exception is redundant and the term is not defined.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- They are by default public except for imported and friend definitions.

requirements.original: Import definitions are by default private.
requirements.canonical: An import statement without an explicit visibility modifier IS private by default.

ambiguity.issue: 'Import definitions' is used for import statements; elsewhere 'import statement' and 'imported definition' are used.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- Import definitions are by default private.

requirements.original: Friend definitions are private only.
requirements.canonical: A friend definition IS private only.

readings: A friend module declaration (friend module X) SHALL only have private visibility.
A definition with friend visibility IS not importable by non-friend modules (i.e. private towards them).
ambiguity.issue: Chosen reading: 'friend definitions' denotes friend module declarations (clause 8.2.4), which can only be private. The term is undefined and could be confused with definitions having friend visibility.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- Friend definitions are private only.

requirements.original: Group definitions are public only.
requirements.canonical: A group definition IS public only.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- Group definitions are public only.

requirements.original: Group definitions are public only.
requirements.canonical: A group definition SHALL NOT be declared with `friend` or `private` visibility.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- Group definitions are public only.

requirements.original: [ public | friend | private ]
requirements.canonical: A visibility modifier HAS the syntax [ `public` | `friend` | `private` ], i.e. it is optional and is one of the keywords `public`, `friend` or `private`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- [ public | friend | private ]

requirements.original: The visibility controls whether a top-level definition or an import statement is importable by another module.
requirements.canonical: The visibility of a top-level definition or an import statement CONTROLS whether it is importable by another module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- The visibility controls whether a top-level definition or an import statement is importable by another module.

requirements.original: A top-level definition or an import statement with public visibility is importable by any other module.
requirements.canonical: A top-level definition or an import statement with public visibility IS importable by any other module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- A top-level definition or an import statement with public visibility is importable by any other module.

requirements.original: A top-level definition or an import statement with friend visibility is importable by friend modules only (see clause 8.2.4).
requirements.canonical: A top-level definition or an import statement with friend visibility IS importable by friend modules only.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- A top-level definition or an import statement with friend visibility is importable by friend modules only (see clause 8.2.4).

requirements.original: A top-level definition or an import statement with private visibility cannot be imported at all.
requirements.canonical: A top-level definition or an import statement with private visibility SHALL NOT be imported by any other module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- A top-level definition or an import statement with private visibility cannot be imported at all.

requirements.original: NOTE: As specified in restriction e) of clause 8.2.3.1, this means that importable definitions are imported together with all information of referenced definitions that are necessary for the usage of the importable definition, even if the referenced definition is private.
requirements.canonical: When an importable definition is imported, all information of referenced definitions necessary for the usage of the importable definition IS imported together with it, even if a referenced definition is private.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- NOTE: As specified in restriction e) of clause 8.2.3.1, this means that importable definitions are imported together with all information of referenced definitions that are necessary for the usage of the importable definition, even if the referenced definition is private.

requirements.original: Only the identifier of the referenced definition is not visible in the importing TTCN-3 module.
requirements.canonical: The identifier of a private referenced definition IS NOT visible in the importing module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- Only the identifier of the referenced definition is not visible in the importing TTCN-3 module.

requirements.original: The visibility of groups is always public.
requirements.canonical: The visibility of a group IS always public.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- The visibility of groups is always public.

requirements.original: The visibility of imported definitions is by default private.
requirements.canonical: The visibility of an imported definition IS private by default.
requirements.condition: no visibility modifier is given for the import statement

readings: An import statement without visibility modifier is private, so the definitions imported by it are not re-exported.
An imported definition itself carries a private visibility in the importing module.
ambiguity.issue: Visibility applies to import statements (s003, table 10); chosen reading: the imported definitions are by default not re-importable from the importing module, as the import statement is private.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- The visibility of imported definitions is by default private.

requirements.original: All other module definitions are by default public.
requirements.canonical: A module definition other than a group or an imported definition IS public by default.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- All other module definitions are by default public.

requirements.original: The visibility of a top-level definition or an import statement defines their importability by another module.
requirements.canonical: The visibility of a top-level definition or an import statement DEFINES its importability by another module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- The visibility of a top-level definition or an import statement defines their importability by another module.

requirements.original: If the top-level definition or the import statement is part of a group, this has no effect on the importability of the module definition.
requirements.canonical: Membership of a top-level definition or an import statement in a group IS NOT affecting the importability of that definition.

readings: Group membership never changes the visibility/importability of the definition (a private definition in a group is not imported by group import).
Group membership has no effect on direct import, but importability via group import is still governed separately.
ambiguity.issue: Chosen reading: the visibility of the definition alone determines importability, including via group import (consistent with table 9).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.5 -- If the top-level definition or the import statement is part of a group, this has no effect on the importability of the module definition.

requirements.original: control StatementBlock
requirements.canonical: The module control part HAS the syntax `control` StatementBlock.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.3 -- control StatementBlock

requirements.original: The shorthand notation is equivalent to a module control function with the same statement block, no parameters, no runs on clause and no return clause (see clause 16.1).
requirements.canonical: The module control part IS equivalent to a module control function with the same statement block, no parameters, no `runs on` clause and no `return` clause.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.3 -- The shorthand notation is equivalent to a module control function with the same statement block, no parameters, no runs on clause and no return clause (see clause 16.1).

requirements.original: NOTE: As the control part is a short hand notation of a control function with the name "control", at most 1 control part can be defined in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 module CAN contain at most one module control part.

readings: A module SHALL NOT contain more than one control part.
A module SHALL NOT contain both a control part and an explicitly declared function named control, nor more than one control part.
ambiguity.issue: The note derives the limit from the name clash; chosen the plain reading (at most one control part). Whether a control part plus an explicit control function is also forbidden is implied but not stated.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.3 -- NOTE: As the control part is a short hand notation of a control function with the name "control", at most 1 control part can be defined in a TTCN-3 module.

requirements.original: When not used as an entry point for execution of the test suite, the module control function can be invoked explicitly in a similar way as a standard function, using the control keyword instead of the identifier.
requirements.canonical: When not used as an entry point for test suite execution, a module control function CAN be invoked explicitly like a function, using the `control` keyword instead of an identifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.3 -- When not used as an entry point for execution of the test suite, the module control function can be invoked explicitly in a similar way as a standard function, using the control keyword instead of the identifier.

requirements.original: In this case, the control keyword may be optionally prefixed with a module identifier followed by a dot.
requirements.canonical: In an explicit invocation of a module control function, the `control` keyword MAY be prefixed with a module identifier followed by a dot.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.3 -- In this case, the control keyword may be optionally prefixed with a module identifier followed by a dot.
